title: Deterministic Verification and a Single‑Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured the verifier-confirmed marginal effect of inserting a deterministic validator plus up to one automated repair (a guarded generate–verify–repair pipeline) on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics we produced one initial candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 intent pairs (confirmatory partition = synthetic/emulation only) and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate as-is) and guarded (run deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if it failed, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); paired contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. We explicitly disclose a preregistration–execution deviation (the preregistration framed a sim‑to‑real emulation vs production-like confirmatory comparison that was not executed; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired guarded−baseline difference on the synthetic/emulation partition) and reconcile provider-call accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and identified in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Stochastic generation raises operational correctness and safety concerns because syntactic errors, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce incorrect or unsafe device-config changes. Prior work proposes interposing deterministic validators and repair loops—generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures—to detect and (sometimes) fix mechanically verifiable defects; surveys and empirical studies report benefits for syntactic and locally checkable errors while noting open challenges for semantic behavior, cross‑vendor fidelity, and adversarial robustness [see Related Work].

Research question and contributions. Framed and preregistered before execution, our confirmatory estimand (as executed) asks: when the same natural-language intent is realized by a single LLM-generated configuration candidate and checked deterministically, what is the paired change in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction when the candidate is accepted as-is (baseline) versus when a deterministic validator plus up to one automated repair (guarded) is applied? Our contributions are: (1) a sealed, preregistered paired experiment using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator on N = 250 intent pairs in a synthetic/emulation partition; (2) exact paired inference under shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the marginal validator+single-repair effect on identical LLM outputs; and (3) an artifact-grounded near‑null primary result together with explicit correction of a preregistration–execution divergence and reconciliation of provider-call accounting.
sections.related_work: Multiple recent surveys and empirical works document the emergence of intent→configuration and LLM-assisted NetOps systems, showing that LLMs can produce draft configurations but typically require verification or human oversight; common error modes include syntax, local-policy violations, and vendor-specific command ordering [A, B, C]. Prior architecture and tool work demonstrates that deterministic checkers (e.g., Batfish-style analyses and header-space approaches) and repair templates reduce mechanically verifiable errors in code and configuration domains [D, E, F]. Work on prompt-injection and retrieval-based attacks motivates filter and verifier layers as partial defenses, but adaptive adversaries remain an open threat. This study situates itself among these lines by experimentally measuring the marginal verifier+single-repair effect on the exact same initial candidate under a preregistered shared_initial_candidate design.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration included multiple partitions (emulation/synthetic, community, production-like) and hypotheses framed at the time included a sim‑to‑real comparison. Deviation disclosure (required correction): the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory comparison (emulation vs production-like topologies) was not executed in this run; instead the executed confirmatory contract applied only to the synthetic/emulation partition and measured baseline vs guarded on the shared candidate. This deviation is logged and reconciled in the archived manifests (preregistration SHA-256 and execution manifest described in the Disclosure Statement).

Task generation, model, and pipeline. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks. For each intent we produced one shared initial candidate using declared model gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). That single candidate was reused to populate both episodes per pair: baseline (accept candidate as-is) and guarded (run deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if the validator failed, permit up to one automated repair call following the preregistered repair template). The adapter_family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the deterministic task generator was deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5.

Shared_initial_candidate and provider-call accounting. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, exactly one initial generation call was made per intent and that candidate was evaluated in both paired episodes. The archived execution manifests reconcile accounting: planned_episode_count = 500 (250 pairs × 2 episodes), completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation calls + 1 repair call). Provider-call auditing recorded stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and condition_counts that label instrumented stage counts rather than independent first-pass generation counts per condition. The deterministic reconciliation artifact in the archive documents these values precisely.

Scoring and statistical analysis. The deterministic validator returned a boolean verifier_pass per episode according to preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rules. The primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar (paired) test on the 2×2 contingency table; we report exact p-value and absolute paired difference with a 95% paired bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) as preregistered. Exclusion and contamination rules (parser-blocking syntax, credential tokens, private-address blocks) were applied deterministically; no trials were excluded in the executed confirmatory run.
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-grounded): planned_episode_count = 500; completed_episode_count = 500; complete_pair_count = 250; model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial + 1 repair). Primary confirmatory outcomes (from archived analysis artifacts analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency table (guarded, baseline): n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.004 (0.4 percentage points). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points), computed with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729 as preregistered. Repair outcomes: the single discordant pair (n10 = 1) was converted to pass by the single permitted repair (repair-conversion = 1 / 250). No preregistered exclusions or contamination flags occurred in the confirmatory partition.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The executed confirmatory test—restricted to the synthetic/emulation partition per the preregistration contract used at run time—did not support the preregistered large sim‑to‑real difference hypothesis because that sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed here. Instead, within the synthetic/emulation partition a near‑null marginal verifier+single-repair effect was observed: modern LLM outputs (gpt-5-mini, with the prompt and task constraints used here) were already largely consistent with the deterministic validator encodings, producing 249/250 initial verifier-passes.

Power and inferential constraint. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass ≈ 0.90 and targeted a 15 percentage-point paired effect; the observed baseline pass (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed, which reduces power to detect small differences. The paired bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an artifact-grounded bound on the possible guarded improvement under this design and these inputs.

Threats to validity. Internal: results depend on prompt templates, declared model, the single-repair policy, and strict shared_initial_candidate semantics. Construct: the deterministic validator checked mechanically verifiable workflow and syntactic properties and did not measure broader semantic/behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, performance). External: confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; community and production-like partitions listed in the preregistration were not executed and remain exploratory. Security: adaptive prompt-injection, retrieval-based attacks, and vendor-specific adversarial vectors were not exercised here. Operational implication: in tightly constrained emulation-style task regimes a GVR guardrail may yield limited marginal verifier gains because the generator already produces validator-consistent candidates; do not generalize beyond the studied partition without partition-specific evidence.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus a single automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate; paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp], p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory comparison was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired guarded−baseline difference on the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, and partition‑specific evaluations remain necessary to establish external generality. All execution manifests, responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived as noted in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system (the AI-run research pipeline) performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration.

Preregistration and immutable prompt references (archived): preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1; preregistration artifact SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede. Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution manifest and analysis artifacts (manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis outputs) are archived in the evidence bundle referenced by those artifacts; the archive contains deterministic_reconciliation and analysis artifacts that document provider-call accounting and stage_counts.

Preregistered design and executed estimand: The preregistration specified multiple partitions including an emulation→production-like sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). This deviation is recorded in the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts in the archive. Provider-call accounting: archived provider_call_audit shows stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial + 1 repair); these values reconcile with completed_episode_count = 500 under shared_initial_candidate semantics and are recorded in the deterministic_reconciliation artifact.

Autonomy and artifact scope: literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting/revision were performed autonomously after the lock. All execution metadata, raw outputs, validation traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced above are archived in the evidence bundle; the Disclosure Statement supplies the immutable master prompt and preregistration hashes rather than duplicating full logs here.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
